news.title: Women's 2027 World Cup tickets go on sale from December
news.lede: Nov 13 : Tickets for next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil will go on sale from December 1, organisers said on Friday, with an initial eight-day sales window opening ahead of the tournament's draw on December 11. • Fans will be able to purchase tickets in categories one, two and three, with prices starting from 30 BRL ($5.32) in category three, depending on the matches selected. • The tournament will offer several ticket packages, including a Brazil Team Pass covering the hosts' three group-stage matches, an Arena Pass providing access to matches at a chosen venue up to the quarter-finals, and a Flex Pass that allows fans to select three eligible games. • FIFA Chief Women's Football Officer Sarai Bareman announced details of the launch at Rio de Janeiro's Maracana Stadium, which will host both the opening match and the final.

news.title: Pelé’s Cause of Death: Brazilian Football King’s Battle With Colon Cancer
news.lede: Pelé, the legendary Brazilian footballer known as “O Rei” (The King), died of complications from colon cancer on December 29, 2022, at the age of 82. The only player to win three FIFA World Cups, Pelé became a global symbol of football, inspiring generations with his extraordinary talent and unforgettable achievements. Yet behind his remarkable career, the final chapter of his life was marked by a serious illness. Diagnosed with colon cancer in September 2021, Pelé underwent surgery and chemotherapy before his condition worsened in 2022.

news.title: Football: Japan in another Brazil test as Moriyasu's reign nears end
news.lede: SINGAPORE - Japan will be out to get back at Brazil in an international friendly in Singapore on Saturday after their World Cup dream came to an early end in the round of 32 in Houston this summer. Manager Hajime Moriyasu is set for the final two games of his eight-plus years in charge of the Samurai Blue after the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia, originally scheduled for early next year, was pushed back to December 2027 amid security concerns in the country. "This will be an opportunity to show the people in Singapore and Asia that Asian nations can compete at the world's top level," Moriyasu told a press conference. "We'll be playing with the same objective (as Brazil) and go for the win.

news.title: US withdrawal from Under-17 World Cup exposes the growing reach of Middle East conflict
news.lede: For young footballers, the opportunity to represent their country at a major international tournament should be one of the highlights of their sporting lives. Instead, the deteriorating security environment in the region has forced American football authorities to reconsider whether participation is worth the potential risks. The decision also raises uncomfortable questions about Qatar’s ability to host major international sporting events at a time when regional instability is increasingly affecting travel, security arrangements and international confidence. The withdrawal comes despite FIFA maintaining that its own security assessment has not changed.

news.title: Japan coach Moriyasu to step down from role after Paraguay friendly
news.lede: Tokyo Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu will step down next week, the country’s football association said Friday, cutting short his tenure in the wake of the 2027 Asian Cup’s postponement. Moriyasu, Japan’s longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa. But the Asian Football Confederation announced last week that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to “exceptional circumstances” in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country. That left Moriyasu in limbo, with Japan Football Association (JFA) chiefs last week declining to clarify when the coaching handover would take place.

news.title: 'Like a World Cup match' - Brazil captain Raphinha expects stern Japan test in Singapore as Hajime Moriyasu's long reign nears its end
news.lede: Stand-in Brazil captain Raphinha anticipates a fierce examination against Japan in Saturday's international friendly in Singapore. The rematch of this summer's World Cup clash in Houston comes as Samurai Blue boss Hajime Moriyasu prepares for the final two games of his eight-year tenure. Stand-in skipper anticipates fierce battle Raphinha will wear both the armband and the iconic number 10 shirt at the Singapore National Stadium with regular skipper Marquinhos sidelined through injury. The Asian side are seeking revenge for their late 2-1 comeback defeat in the World Cup round of 32 in June .
